Zeeland storm surge, Jan 1976 — interpolated flood-risk map (5-min model)

A continuous risk surface over the whole visible area: each gauge contributes a soft gaussian impulse, so the surface fades to nothing away from every gauge instead of extrapolating - blue is calm, red is at or above each gauge's own POT/EVT flood threshold (risk = |observed − predicted| / threshold, so every gauge's very different natural variability is normalized onto the same 0-1+ scale). Each gauge's contribution lingers and decays with a 3-hour half-life rather than switching on and off hour to hour, so a real spike fades out gradually instead of spiking and vanishing. Drag the slider or press play to scrub through the event.

calm  →  at/above flood threshold
Model: zeeland_flood_eval_5min (5-min resample, CUTS+ causal discovery + hold-out 1-step prediction). Risk = max(|observed − predicted| this hour, previous risk × decay) / that gauge's own POT threshold (cm), decay = 0.5^(1/3) per hour (3-hour half-life) - a peak-hold-with-decay filter, computed once at build time from the trained checkpoint's saved residual z-scores and POT/EVT threshold refit at risk=0.001 / initial_level=0.99 / num_candidates=100 (the best-F1 point from sweep_pot_params.py). The surface is a gaussian-kernel interpolation across the 40 gauges (of 77 total) with enough validation data to fit a threshold at all, and is drawn over both land and water - the model only ever had Zeeland's own gauges to work with, so risk away from them is extrapolated, not measured; the surrounding Dutch/Belgian coastline is shown for geographic context only, not scored. Event window (1976-01-03 14:00 → 1976-01-05 18:00) shown as a red band on the slider track. Coastline: ~1,700 real OpenStreetMap natural=water bodies across the whole visible area (every named lake, estuary, harbor and canal OSM has polygon-mapped here - not just Zeeland's), over a Dutch-municipality land fill (CBS/Kadaster); Natural Earth's open-ocean outline fills in only where neither of those has any data (mainly the open North Sea itself), so its coarser resolution is never visible next to real coastline. A few major tidal channels - the Westerschelde, Nieuwe Waterweg, Nieuwe Maas and Scheur - aren't water-tagged as areas in OSM at all (confirmed directly: they're mapped only as waterway=river lines), so they still read as land rather than water.
